record.paper_title: A List of Problems on the Reverse Mathematics of Ramsey Theory on the Rado Graph and on Infinite, Finitely Branching Trees
record.original_question: Over RCA0, are the following four principles equivalent: (A) the Halpern-Lauchli Theorem for any finite number of trees; (B) Milliken Ramsey theorem for strong trees on one finitely branching infinite tree with no terminal nodes; (C) the canonical partition theorem for colorings of a fixed finite graph inside the Rado graph; and (D) for every k at least 2, the Rado graph has the rainbow Ramsey property for k-bounded colorings?

evidence.quote: The following implications are known as ZFC, or even just ZF, results: with (A) => (B) => (C) => (D).
(1) Are any of (A) - (D) equivalent over RCA0?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the framework of reverse mathematics over the base system RCA₀ (Recursive Comprehension Axiom). Consider the following four combinatorial principles.

(A) Halpern–Läuchli Theorem (finite product version): For every finite sequence T₁,…,T_d of finitely branching infinite trees with no terminal nodes, and every finite coloring of the level product ⋃_{n} (T₁(n)×⋯×T_d(n)) (where T_i(n) denotes the n-th level of T_i), there exist strong subtrees S_i ⊆ T_i (each S_i is an infinite subtree all of whose nodes at the k-th level of S lie on a common level of T_i, and which branches fully in T_i) such that the induced level product ⋃_{n}(S₁(n)×⋯×S_d(n)) is monochromatic.

(B) Milliken's Ramsey theorem for strong trees on one tree: For every finitely branching infinite tree T with no terminal nodes, every finite k, and every finite coloring of the set of strong subtrees of T of height k, there is an infinite strong subtree S ⊆ T all of whose strong subtrees of height k receive the same color.

(C) Canonical partition theorem for the Rado graph: Let R denote the Rado graph (the countable random graph). For every finite graph G and every coloring (with arbitrarily many colors) of the set of copies of G in R, there exists an isomorphic copy R' ⊆ R of R such that the coloring restricted to copies of G inside R' depends only on a canonical equivalence relation determined by G.

(D) Rainbow Ramsey property for the Rado graph: For every integer k ≥ 2, every finite graph G, and every k-bounded coloring of the copies of G in R (a coloring in which each color is used on at most k copies of G), there is an isomorphic copy R' ⊆ R of R such that all copies of G inside R' receive pairwise distinct colors.

It is known (provably in ZF) that (A) ⇒ (B) ⇒ (C) ⇒ (D). Question: Are any two of the principles (A), (B), (C), (D) equivalent over RCA₀? In particular, is the full chain (A) ⇔ (B) ⇔ (C) ⇔ (D) provable over RCA₀?
